title: Staggered weight diffusion and KV probing for stepped traffic onboarding
creator: Diego Alvarez
description:
Goal: reduce cold-start surface and improve predictable throughput during stepped traffic onramps for Dedicated fleets by combining a staggered weight diffusion loader with lightweight KV-probing probes and an admission-aware slow-start throttler.

Background: current warm pool strategies either fully prefetch weights (high cost, long tail for many models) or rely on best-effort background hydration which causes throughput cliffs during sudden tenant ramps. We need a middle ground that guarantees contracted throughput tiers while minimizing memory and network spikes across GPUs.

Proposal (high level):
1) Staggered weight diffusion: instead of atomically loading an entire model snapshot onto a node, we stream parameter shards in ranked residency order (hot slices first) across a small cohort of nodes. Each cohort is sized to the requested throughput and admits traffic in soft-sliced increments. This diffuses network and disk I/O and reduces peak allocation churn.
2) KV probing (micro-primes): after the first hot slices are resident, run micro-requests (short synthetic prompts representing typical tenant distributions) to warm per-tenant KV caches to a target hit-rate threshold. These probes are bounded by token budget and backed off if they impact live latency. Probes use sampled traces from the tenant's recent traffic (or synthetic traces for new tenants).
3) Admission-aware slow-start throttler: couple the autoscaler admission with a slow-start algorithm that ramps concurrent in-flight requests and batch sizes based on observed fill-rate and KV hit-rate. This prevents oversubscription and gives the diffusion process time to fully converge.

Key trade-offs considered:
- Full prefetching vs. diffusion: prefetch guarantees readiness but increases memory footprint and cost. Diffusion reduces footprint but requires careful admission control. We chose diffusion for cost-sensitive fleets with throughput guarantees because it provides a controlled ramp with lower steady-state reservation.
- Synthetic probes vs. live shadowing: synthetic probes are cheaper and safe for privacy but may miss tail contexts. We'll start with synthetic probes seeded from anonymized samples and add optional controlled shadowing for high-SLA customers.

Metrics and SLOs:
- Target: reduce median cold-start linearization time from ~6s to <1.5s for hot-path responses during an onramp.
- Target: 95th percentile request latency during 3-minute stepped ramp should not exceed steady-state SLO by more than 2x.
- KV probe target: reach 75% KV hit-rate for common prefixes within the first 60s of admission.
- Cost budget: keep additional network egress and disk I/O for warmup < 12% of a tenant's monthly committed usage on average.

Design details and APIs:
- New fleet config fields: warmup.cohort_size, warmup.slice_size_mb, warmup/probe_token_budget, warmup/admission_profile (conservative | balanced | aggressive).
- Admission events emitted to Console: warmup.start, warmup.slice_loaded, warmup.kv_probe_status, warmup.completed. Include per-tenant metrics for cohort id and probe hit-rate.
- Rollout toggle: feature flag dedicated.warmup.staggered with canary targeting internal test tenants.

Rollout plan:
1) Unit + integration tests for diffusion pipeline and KV-probe simulator (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6789).
2) Canary: internal staging tenants + 3 low-volume customers with close monitoring dashboards (dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-inference.com/d/kwarm/warmup-cohort-insights).
3) Gradual enablement on new Dedicated allocations; opt-in for existing contracts with SLA guardrails.

Runbook and rollback:
- If p95 latency or error rate for a cohort exceeds thresholds, abort new admissions, mark cohort read-only, and trigger emergency fallback to conventional dedicated fallback model variant (smaller but fully resident).
- Rollback step: toggle feature flag off, gracefully drain cohorts, and revert autoscaler profiles.

Telemetry and validation:
- Add event counters and histograms (cohort_load_duration_ms, kv_probe_hit_rate, diffusion_throughput_rps).
- A/B experiment with 10% of ramped traffic to compare cost-per-token and latency.

Open design questions / next steps:
- Exact heuristics for slice ordering (layer-wise vs. shard hotness) — prefer layer-hotness for transformer heads commonality; need microbenchmarks.
- Tenant trace sampling cadence and privacy guardrails — coordinate with Security/Privacy.
- Memory residency guarantees for mixed-model nodes — evaluate eviction policy integration with existing residency allocator.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood-inference.com/display/WARM/Staggered+Diffusion+Design
- PR with prototype loader and probe harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6789
- Load test results (internal): https://internal-redwood/storage/warmup/loadtest/2026-03-05/results.csv

Acceptance criteria:
- Integration tests pass and prototype validated in staging under synthetic stepped ramps.
- Canary shows improved cost-per-commit and no more than 1.5x p95 latency inflation for 99% of cohorts.
- Console emits warmup events and KV hit-rate metrics for cohort-level inspection.
